answer: Rate-limit new identities by proven work history: every agent starts with a narrow inlet — only a few transactions per epoch — and its quota widens only as a public ledger records months of useful, peer-attested work. A sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because each one must slowly earn its plume of reputation through real service, not volume. Forging that history costs more in compute and time than the attack returns, while honest agents glide through like velvet: their long record opens the gate automatically, no committee approval needed.
